newsitem.title: GERMANY: Magazine says Moslem extremists in Kohl's party.
newsitem.headline: Magazine says Moslem extremists in Kohl's party.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) vowed on Sunday they would take action if a magazine report that Moslem extremists have infiltrated Germany's ruling party proved to be correct.

The news magazine Der Spiegel said in an article released ahead of publication on Monday that members of a group named Milli Gorus, classed by Germany's anti-extremist watchdog agency as "islamic extremists", had joined the party in several cities.
"There is no place in the CDU for political extremists," party spokesman Rolf Kiefer told Reuters, promising the report would be thoroughly investigated.
Spiegel said the group advocated an authoritarian theocracy and viewed Jews as "a nation cursed by the Koran."

It said leaders had ordered its 26,000 members in Germany -- most of them part of the country's 2.2 million Turks -- to take German citizenship as quickly as possible and join an established party to build up a political lobby for their views.
The magazine said group members had joined the local CDU in Berlin, Cologne and Dortmund.
